options.D: To stop the sudden breakdown of muscle tissue throughout the body

explanation: Elevated potassium levels severely affect the electrical system of the heart, leading to fatal cardiac arrhythmias if left untreated. [learn more](GNS213_U4_T6#GNS213_U4_T6_h5)

question: What famous global health goal was established at the 1978 Alma-Ata conference?

options.A: Eradication of Malaria by 1985
options.B: Universal Hospital Access by 1990
options.C: Health for All by the Year 2000
options.D: Free Tertiary Care for Every Citizen

explanation: The Alma-Ata conference set the ambitious global target of achieving 'Health for All by the Year 2000' through primary health care. [learn more](GNS124_U1_T2#GNS124_U1_T2_h3)

question: What is the main dietary focus when caring for a patient with high blood pressure (hypertension)?

options.A: Sodium restriction
options.B: Zero fluid consumption
options.C: High protein loading
options.D: Unlimited sugar intake

explanation: You know this! Cutting down on salt (sodium) helps reduce fluid retention and lowers pressure inside the blood vessels.

question: Which chamber of the heart pumps oxygenated blood into the aorta?

options.A: Right ventricle
options.B: Left atrium
options.C: Left ventricle
options.D: Right atrium

explanation: The left ventricle has a thick muscular wall designed to pump blood through the aorta to the rest of the body. [learn more](GNS111_U2_T4#GNS111_U2_T4_h1)

question: What is the main purpose of advance care planning?

options.A: To ensure patient wishes guide future treatment
options.B: To let healthcare providers make all choices
options.C: To speed up the legal probate process
options.D: To reduce hospital cleaning costs

explanation: Spot on! Advance care planning makes sure the patient's voice is heard and respected, even if they can no longer speak for themselves later on.

question: What is a major effect of malnutrition in school children?

options.A: Impaired learning capacity and weakened immunity
options.B: Enhanced resistance to common viral infections
options.C: Rapid acceleration in physical height and bone density
options.D: Increased ability to focus for long hours

explanation: That's right! Without proper nutrients, the body and brain struggle, leading to poor concentration, tiredness, and frequent sickness.

question: Why do certain long-term medications often lead to bad tooth decay?

options.A: They chemically melt away the outer shell of the teeth
options.B: They make patients crave and eat too many sugary sweets
options.C: They permanently freeze the jaw muscles so chewing stops
options.D: They cause dry mouth, taking away the protective washing power of saliva

explanation: Many drugs cause dry mouth (xerostomia). Without enough saliva to wash things away, food acids stay behind and tooth decay takes over.

question: How would you describe a delusion?

options.A: A complete lack of emotional expression
options.B: A fixed, false belief resistant to logic
options.C: A sudden inability to speak any words
options.D: A sensory experience without external stimuli

explanation: Well done! A delusion is a strong belief that stays stuck in the person's mind, even when clear facts show it isn't true.

question: What is the main purpose of performing Leopold's maneuvers during an antenatal visit?

options.A: To check if the mother has a urinary tract infection
options.B: To determine fetal position, size, and presentation
options.C: To measure the exact amount of blood in the body
options.D: To find out when the baby will start walking

explanation: Leopold's maneuvers use gentle hand movements on the abdomen to feel how the baby is lying. [learn more](GNS225_U3_T8#GNS225_U3_T8_h5)

question: Why is working hand-in-hand with traditional and religious leaders so helpful for contact tracing in local communities?

options.A: They personally conduct laboratory PCR testing for infectious diseases
options.B: They hold the trust of the people and help dispel harmful rumors
options.C: They are legally certified epidemiologists trained in data analysis
options.D: They provide the financial budget needed to buy hospital beds

explanation: Amazing! Local leaders are deeply trusted by community members, so when they support public health efforts, the community is much more willing to cooperate.

question: A patient with stable blood pressure comes to a clinic after losing their home in a disaster, and their blood pressure is suddenly very high. Why?

options.A: An intentional overdose of emergency relief food
options.B: Exposure to cold weather causing elevated heart rates
options.C: Disruption of routine medication access and extreme environmental stress
options.D: Sudden permanent cure of their baseline hypertension

explanation: Spot on! Disasters cut off regular medications and create heavy stress, which easily triggers spikes in conditions like high blood pressure.

question: What is the main job of a Quality Assurance (QA) Committee in a hospital?

options.A: Hiring and firing clinical staff members
options.B: Managing the hospital budget and staff salaries
options.C: Checking and improving the standard of patient care
options.D: Buying new medical equipment for the wards

explanation: You got this! A QA committee is basically the hospital's safety and quality champion, making sure patients get the best care possible.

question: What is a major risk of relying on virtual health communities?

options.A: Members are legally required to pay monthly subscription fees
options.B: Unverified medical advice and misinformation can spread rapidly
options.C: Patients will completely lose access to their local doctors
options.D: It guarantees that patients will never experience illness again

explanation: Spot on! Anyone can post online, so fake news and harmful health remedies can easily trick people if they aren't careful.

question: Why is it dangerous to place a septic drain field too close to a shallow drinking water well?

options.A: Roots from nearby trees will block the water pipes completely
options.B: Liquid effluent can seep into the groundwater and spread pathogens
options.C: The weight of the water well can crush the underground septic tank
options.D: The smell of the drain field will ruin the taste of the well water

explanation: If a drain field is too close to a well, untreated wastewater can travel through the soil and contaminate the underground drinking water with dangerous bacteria and viruses.

question: Why is the Trait theory considered a bit limited in modern nursing?

options.A: It requires every nurse to have advanced surgical training
options.B: It focuses too much on patient vital signs instead of administration
options.C: It ignores how leadership skills can be learned and shaped by situations
options.D: It proves that nurses never make good ward managers

explanation: While personal traits matter, Trait theory forgets that anyone can learn leadership skills and adapt to different situations on the ward.

question: Which group of occupational lung diseases is caused by inhaling mineral dusts like silica and asbestos?

options.A: Pneumoconiosis
options.B: Simple Bronchitis
options.C: Occupational Asthma
options.D: Hypersensitivity Pneumonitis

explanation: Pneumoconiosis is the medical term for fibrotic lung diseases caused by the accumulation of mineral dusts in the lungs. [learn more](GNS213_U2_T8#GNS213_U2_T8_h3)

question: How do pests like rats and flies make unmanaged hospital rubbish so dangerous?

options.A: They physically carry pathogens from the waste back into living and treatment areas
options.B: They consume all the toxic chemicals and render the waste completely harmless
options.C: They increase the rate at which biodegradable plastics break down in the sun
options.D: They serve as reliable biological indicators for routine environmental audits

explanation: Exactly! Pests feed on infectious waste and can transfer dangerous germs right back into patient care areas. Good job catching that!

question: Why do doctors often give corticosteroids to a mum facing early labor?

options.A: To accelerate fetal lung maturity and reduce breathing difficulties
options.B: To permanently stop all uterine contractions from happening
options.C: To prevent postpartum hemorrhage after delivery
options.D: To lower the mother's blood glucose levels rapidly

explanation: Steroids give a fantastic boost to the baby's developing lungs, helping them avoid serious breathing trouble if they decide to arrive early.

question: Why should community midwives collaborate with traditional birth attendants instead of ignoring them?

options.A: Traditional birth attendants outnumber all trained doctors in cities.
options.B: TBAs are often trusted first-line care providers in rural areas.
options.C: TBAs have advanced surgical degrees from university hospitals.
options.D: Government policy requires TBAs to manage major surgical operations.

explanation: Because many women naturally seek out TBAs first, working with them helps redirect high-risk cases to formal health facilities much faster. [learn more](GNS225_U3_T14#GNS225_U3_T14_h7)

question: What is the major danger of failing to treat puerperal sepsis promptly?

options.A: Immediate closure of the fallopian tubes
options.B: Development of chronic gestational diabetes
options.C: Permanent discoloration of the skin and hair
options.D: Progression to septic shock and multi-organ failure

explanation: An infection left unchecked in the uterus won't just stay there—it can spread through the whole body, causing a dangerous drop in blood pressure and organ failure.

question: When a mother of young children is admitted to the hospital for major surgery, what is the most likely effect on her family?

options.A: Family members will immediately stop working to stay in the hospital room.
options.B: Household expenses will decrease due to reduced grocery shopping.
options.C: The family structure remains entirely unchanged during hospital stays.
options.D: Family roles must be rearranged to cover childcare and household duties.

explanation: Spot on! When a key caregiver falls ill, family routines get disrupted, forcing other members to step up and handle chores and childcare.

question: A patient with unsteady balance and dizziness is admitted to the medical ward. What is the most immediate safety risk to prevent?

options.A: A wrong-site surgical procedure
options.B: A severe hospital-acquired infection
options.C: A physical fall leading to injury
options.D: An accidental medication overdose

explanation: Unsteadiness and dizziness directly increase the likelihood of slips and falls, making fall precautions the priority intervention for this patient. [learn more](GNS312_U5_T5#GNS312_U5_T5_h3)

question: Which quick bedside test must you do immediately for any unconscious patient?

options.A: Electroencephalogram
options.B: Blood glucose test
options.C: Complete blood count
options.D: Chest X-ray examination

explanation: Always check the sugar first! Low blood sugar can mimic a major stroke or brain injury, and it's super easy to test and fix right at the bedside.

question: Which attitude is most important for a nurse during post-abortion counseling?

options.A: Non-judgmental and empathetic
options.B: Skeptical and questioning
options.C: Indifferent and detached
options.D: Strictly authoritative and firm

explanation: Being warm, kind, and non-judgmental builds trust, making the patient feel safe to share their worries and ask questions.

question: What does the 'planning' function of management involve?

options.A: Punishing staff members for clinical errors
options.B: Deciding ahead of time what needs to be done and who will do it
options.C: Ordering medical supplies from external vendors
options.D: Evaluating individual lab results at the bedside

explanation: Planning is simply looking ahead, setting goals, and figuring out your game plan before the shift gets crazy.

question: What is an outlier in a research dataset?

options.A: A missing patient file that was never collected
options.B: A category label used for nominal variables
options.C: The exact mathematical average of a frequency table
options.D: An extreme value that sits far away from other data points

explanation: Outliers are data entries that are unusually high or low compared to the vast majority of the observations in the dataset. [learn more](GNS224_U2_T2#GNS224_U2_T2_h7)

question: Which hormone keeps the uterus relaxed and quiet throughout most of pregnancy?

options.A: Oxytocin
options.B: Estrogen
options.C: Prostaglandin
options.D: Progesterone

explanation: Progesterone is like a chill pill for the uterus, keeping the muscles relaxed until it's time to meet the baby.

question: Which of these is NOT a common complication of unmanaged maternal distress?

options.A: Increased need for emergency Caesarean birth
options.B: Postpartum psychological trauma
options.C: Dysfunctional or prolonged labour
options.D: Permanent loss of maternal vision

explanation: Vision loss doesn't happen just from stress during labour. The other options are very real risks when distress isn't managed!

question: What two signs tell us a mother is truly in preterm labour?

options.A: Regular contractions and progressive cervical change
options.B: Complete rupture of membranes and heavy bleeding
options.C: Severe headache and blurred vision in the third trimester
options.D: High blood pressure and sudden swelling of the feet

explanation: Spotting true labour means looking for both regular tummy tightening (contractions) and signs that the cervix is actually opening up. Great job learning the clinical markers!

question: Why do established rectovaginal fistulas rarely heal on their own?

options.A: The tract becomes lined with epithelium
options.B: Bowel movements constantly stretch the perineum
options.C: Vaginal acidity dissolves new tissue growth
options.D: Continuous high blood pressure prevents clotting

explanation: Once epithelial tissue lines the abnormal passage, the body treats the tract as a normal surface, preventing natural closure. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T13#GNS216_U5_T13_h2)

question: What might a nurse notice during a pelvic exam of someone who has Type II FGM?

options.A: Enlargement of internal reproductive organs beyond normal size
options.B: Complete closure of the vaginal opening with a thick bridge
options.C: Partial or total absence of the clitoris and labia minora
options.D: Total absence of the uterus and ovaries on palpation

explanation: Correct! Type II FGM involves removing the clitoris along with the labia minora, which can be clearly observed during an examination.

question: Which clinical observation around the umbilical stump indicates the development of omphalitis?

options.A: Redness of the skin and foul-smelling discharge
options.B: A dry, black, and completely shriveled stump
options.C: Natural separation of the cord after one week
options.D: A small drop of clear blood upon diaper removal

explanation: Spreading redness, swelling, and pus or bad smells around the navel are classic signs of a dangerous umbilical infection. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T51#GNS214_U1_T51_h5)

question: A patient vomits severely just two hours after eating leftover rice. What is the most likely cause?

options.A: Primary viral lung infection
options.B: Food-borne intoxication
options.C: Parasitic bowel infestation
options.D: Chronic autoimmune reaction

explanation: Spot on! That super-short window between eating and vomiting is the classic signature of a food toxin (intoxication). Keep up the fantastic work!

question: What is the safest way to carry a full medical waste bag?

options.A: Drag it across the floor to avoid straining your back muscles
options.B: Hug it tightly against the chest to balance the heavy weight
options.C: Lift it by the neck and keep it away from the body
options.D: Balance it on the shoulder while walking to the disposal site

explanation: Hold the bag by its neck away from your body. That way, if a hidden needle pokes through the plastic, it won't hit you!

question: What is a common immediate complication right after FGM is performed?

options.A: Rheumatoid joint inflammation
options.B: Gestational diabetes mellitus
options.C: Early onset menopause
options.D: Severe hemorrhage and shock

explanation: That's right! Cutting sensitive genital tissue leads to heavy bleeding and intense pain, often causing acute shock right after the procedure. [learn more](GNS312_U1_T8#GNS312_U1_T8_h2)

question: What are the two main parts of the human immune system?

options.A: Primary and secondary defense
options.B: Innate and adaptive immunity
options.C: Cellular and humoral barriers
options.D: Active and passive antibodies

explanation: Great job! The immune system has two main teams: innate immunity (the fast, born-with-it guards) and adaptive immunity (the smart specialists that learn to fight specific germs over time). You've got this!

question: What is the medical term for menstrual bleeding that is unusually heavy or lasts too long?

options.A: Metrorrhagia
options.B: Menorrhagia
options.C: Dysmenorrhea
options.D: Amenorrhea

explanation: Menorrhagia is the term for extra heavy or long periods. You will see this often in clinical practice when patients complain about soaking through pads too quickly.

question: A fasting blood sugar test is most commonly used to check for which condition?

options.A: Diabetes mellitus
options.B: Iron deficiency anemia
options.C: Hypothyroidism
options.D: Chronic kidney disease

explanation: Spot on! Fasting blood sugar is one of the quickest and most common ways doctors and nurses screen for diabetes mellitus.

question: You are caring for three patients who all have the exact same stubborn, drug-resistant bacterial infection. What is the best step to take?

options.A: Put them all together in the same designated room (cohorting)
options.B: Let them share personal items like towels freely
options.C: Move all three patients out to the general waiting area
options.D: Stop giving them antibiotics to see if their bodies fight it alone

explanation: Grouping (or cohorting) patients with the same bug keeps them together safely and protects all the other uninfected patients on the ward!

question: Why might a patient with severe carbon monoxide poisoning show a falsely normal or high oxygen saturation reading on a pulse oximeter?

options.A: Carbon monoxide makes the pulse rate extremely fast
options.B: Cold fingers stop the machine from recording low numbers
options.C: Bright lights in the room interfere with the infrared sensors
options.D: The device reads carbon monoxide attached to hemoglobin just like oxygen

explanation: Standard pulse oximeters cannot distinguish between oxygen and carbon monoxide bound to hemoglobin, leading to dangerously misleading high readings. [learn more](GNS212_U4_T6#GNS212_U4_T6_h7)

question: Which nursing action compromises the accuracy of a fluid balance chart?

options.A: Waiting until the end of the shift to guess and write down intake amounts
options.B: Involving the patient and family in reporting oral drinks
options.C: Converting all cup and bowl volumes into milliliters promptly
options.D: Notifying the doctor immediately about a sudden drop in urine output

explanation: Relying on memory causes missed entries and incorrect data that jeopardize patient safety. [learn more](GNS122_U1_T19#GNS122_U1_T19_h8)

question: Why does the pulse oximeter algorithm focus specifically on pulsating arterial blood?

options.A: To calculate the exact speed of blood flow through the heart valves
options.B: To prevent the sensor probe from overheating during long monitoring sessions
options.C: To measure the total volume of red blood cells in the bone marrow
options.D: To ignore constant light absorption from skin, bone, and non-pulsating tissue

explanation: Focusing on the pulse wave lets the machine isolate arterial blood from surrounding static tissues like skin and bone. [learn more](GNS212_U4_T6#GNS212_U4_T6_h3)

question: What is the main reason for routine health checkups before hiring food handlers?

options.A: To detect communicable diseases before workers start preparing food
options.B: To assess how well workers can handle high-stress kitchen environments
options.C: To determine the correct salary grade for each new kitchen employee
options.D: To test the physical strength and endurance of kitchen staff

explanation: Screenings catch infectious illnesses early so sick or asymptomatic workers don't spread germs to customers. Brilliant!

question: Which of these is NOT a typical chronic condition that threatens an older adult's independence?

options.A: Mild seasonal allergies
options.B: Diabetic nerve damage
options.C: Heart failure
options.D: Stroke

explanation: That's right! While allergies can be annoying, they don't cause long-term disability like major strokes, heart issues, or nerve damage do.

question: Which types of medications most commonly increase the risk of falls in older adults?

options.A: Multivitamins
options.B: Topical antifungal creams
options.C: Sedatives and antihypertensives
options.D: Vitamin C supplements

explanation: Drugs that cause dizziness, sleepiness, or sudden drops in blood pressure can easily lead to a fall. Always keep an eye on safety!

question: Using the Rule of Nines, what percentage of the total body surface area does an adult's entire front chest and abdomen (anterior trunk) cover?

options.A: 36 percent
options.B: 18 percent
options.C: 9 percent
options.D: 27 percent

explanation: The Rule of Nines is a classic! The front trunk is 18 percent, and the back trunk is also 18 percent. Easy points for your exams!

question: Why are maternal complications during childbirth considered so dangerous?

options.A: They only occur in women with a known history of chronic illness
options.B: They are completely preventable with strict bed rest during pregnancy
options.C: They usually respond slowly to standard emergency medical treatments
options.D: They develop suddenly and can quickly become fatal without prompt care

explanation: Complications like severe bleeding can start out of nowhere. That is why quick action from a skilled nurse is such a lifesaver!

question: What is a key everyday duty for health workers when it comes to food policy?

options.A: Writing the national budget for farm machinery
options.B: Designing state highways for food transport trucks
options.C: Conducting infant growth monitoring to spot early signs of malnutrition
options.D: Issuing business licenses to big food factories

explanation: As health workers, we put policy into action right at the clinic by checking children's growth and catching malnutrition early.

question: Why are children with sickle cell anaemia at a much higher risk of severe bacterial infections?

options.A: Low dietary iron intake weakens the entire immune system from birth
options.B: The bone marrow stops producing white blood cells to make more sickled cells
options.C: Repeated blood vessel blockages eventually damage and destroy spleen function
options.D: Abnormal haemoglobin coats bacteria and prevents immune cells from seeing them

explanation: The spleen filters bacteria and helps fight infections, but repeated sickling clogs its vessels until it stops working entirely, a process called auto-splenectomy. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T16#GNS214_U1_T16_h3)

question: Which cultural factor often contributes to severe maternal health issues in rural areas?

options.A: Excessive use of modern antenatal care clinics in the first trimester
options.B: Reliance on unskilled traditional attendants for complicated deliveries
options.C: Early mandatory retirement for women of childbearing age
options.D: Over-consumption of iron-rich foods due to local cultural taboos

explanation: When women rely on birth attendants who cannot manage emergencies, getting specialized medical care is dangerously delayed. Community health education helps bridge this gap!

question: What is a common result of supportive and transformational leadership on a hospital ward?

options.A: More communication breakdowns among health workers
options.B: Higher rates of preventable patient falls
options.C: Increased staff turnover and frequent nurse burnout
options.D: Lower medication errors and higher staff satisfaction

explanation: Supportive leadership builds a safe reporting culture and teamwork, which reduces errors and keeps nurses happy. [learn more](GST321_U3_T3#GST321_U3_T3_h7)

question: What is the primary mechanism behind a fat embolism following a long bone fracture?

options.A: Immobility causes fat cells under the skin to melt into the bloodstream
options.B: Infection at the fracture site turns local soft tissues into fatty deposits
options.C: The body stores extra dietary fat in broken bones during the healing phase
options.D: Fat droplets from the bone marrow enter open blood vessels and travel to the lungs

explanation: When a large long bone breaks, yellow bone marrow fat can escape into damaged blood vessels, creating emboli that block small vessels in the lungs and brain. [learn more](GNS221_U3_T13#GNS221_U3_T13_h6)

question: A primary health clinic in a rural Nigerian community wants to improve antenatal care attendance. What is the best first step based on local health system realities?

options.A: Report all pregnant women who miss clinic dates to the police
options.B: Consult village development committees and local women leaders
options.C: Close the clinic until pregnant women start coming on their own
options.D: Wait for federal funds to build a brand new modern hospital

explanation: Engaging trusted local structures helps identify why women are not attending and builds culturally acceptable solutions. [learn more](GNS124_U4_T4#GNS124_U4_T4_h3)

question: Why do doctors cap a tracheostomy tube for a test period before finally removing it?

options.A: To make the outer cannula fit more tightly
options.B: To prevent any saliva from pooling in the throat
options.C: To test if the patient can breathe adequately through the upper airway
options.D: To check if the suction machine is working properly

explanation: Capping blocks the tube so air is forced back through the nose and mouth. It's a great test run to prove the patient can handle breathing normally before the tube comes out!

question: What simple tool do nurses use to plot a child's weight against their age during clinic visits?

options.A: Patient temperature log
options.B: Road to Health chart
options.C: Blood pressure record sheet
options.D: Surgical safety checklist

explanation: You nailed it! The Road to Health chart is a handy visual tool we use everywhere to track how well a child is growing over time.

question: What is a major benefit of peer support groups for people with physical disabilities?

options.A: Enforcing strict government compliance with building codes
options.B: Providing a safe space to share coping strategies and reduce loneliness
options.C: Offering specialized surgical treatments for mobility restoration
options.D: Replacing the need for family interaction entirely

explanation: Well done! Peer groups are wonderful because meeting others facing similar challenges helps kill loneliness and shares great life tips.

question: What is the main difference between normal (physiological) and abnormal (pathological) moulding?

options.A: Physiological moulding is normal and reversible, while pathological moulding involves excessive, damaging forces
options.B: Physiological moulding only happens in premature babies, whereas pathological moulding happens at term
options.C: Pathological moulding causes soft swelling while physiological moulding causes hard ridges
options.D: Pathological moulding involves bone fractures and permanent shape changes

explanation: Spot on! Normal moulding happens in almost every birth and goes away on its own. Pathological moulding comes from extreme, harsh pressure that can cause harm.

question: What is the primary imaging test used to confirm and evaluate a suspected bone fracture?

options.A: Endoscopy
options.B: Echocardiogram
options.C: Electrocardiogram
options.D: X-ray

explanation: X-rays are quick, accessible, and provide clear pictures of bone architecture, making them the standard first choice for diagnosing fractures. [learn more](GNS222_U1_T10#GNS222_U1_T10_h6)

question: What is a very normal emotional reaction for patients waiting to find out if they have cancer?

options.A: Uncontrolled physical hunger
options.B: Extreme happiness and relief
options.C: Intense anxiety and shock
options.D: Complete emotional numbness

explanation: Waiting for big health news is terrifying. Shock and heavy anxiety are very common reactions that nurses need to be ready to support.

question: A patient with severe anxiety is breathing very fast and deep (hyperventilating). What happens to their blood gas values?

options.A: Decreased carbon dioxide levels and increased pH
options.B: Increased bicarbonate retention by the lung tissue
options.C: Increased carbon dioxide levels and decreased pH
options.D: Decreased oxygen saturation in the arterial plasma

explanation: Fast breathing blows off too much $CO_2$. Less $CO_2$ means less acid in the blood, which causes the pH to rise (alkalosis). Makes sense, right?

question: Which area in the TSSU uses negative air pressure?

options.A: Preparation zone
options.B: Decontamination zone
options.C: Sterile storage zone
options.D: Packaging zone

explanation: Spot on! The dirty (decontamination) zone has negative air pressure so that air flows inward, trapping germs and stopping them from floating out into cleaner rooms.

question: Which mental health condition is frequently missed in older adults because it often hides behind physical complaints like body aches?

options.A: Acute delirium
options.B: Bipolar mania
options.C: Depression
options.D: Schizophrenia

explanation: Good to know! Depression in seniors is easy to miss because they might talk about constant tiredness or aches instead of feeling sad.

question: What is the term for the grief family members feel *before* a terminally ill loved one actually passes away?

options.A: Anticipatory grief
options.B: Perceived grief
options.C: Complicated grief
options.D: Masked grief

explanation: Anticipatory grief happens ahead of an expected loss, which actually gives loved ones a bit of time to process their emotions early.

question: Why do community health nurses look at accidents as things we can prevent rather than just 'bad luck'?

options.A: Because bad luck cannot be studied scientifically
options.B: Because most accidents follow preventable patterns
options.C: Because hospitals profit directly from treating injuries
options.D: Because government policies cause all accidents

explanation: Spotting accidents as preventable events helps us design safety steps that keep our communities safe and injury-free!

question: What should be prepared ahead of time in case an emergency happens during a home birth?

options.A: Traditional dancing costumes for visitors
options.B: Transport arrangements and emergency contact numbers
options.C: Extra cooking utensils for the family
options.D: A formal letter of apology to the hospital

explanation: Having transport and contacts ready prevents deadly delays when seconds count during an unexpected crisis. [learn more](GNS225_U3_T9#GNS225_U3_T9_h7)

question: Which of the following is NOT a standard nursing consideration related to postpartum endocrine changes?

options.A: Monitoring for sudden increases in maternal blood pressure caused by rising placental hormone levels
options.B: Observing for successful milk let-down reflex stimulated by infant suckling and oxytocin
options.C: Reassuring the mother about normal physiological changes during her hospital recovery
options.D: Assessing for signs of postpartum mood changes linked to rapid estrogen and progesterone withdrawal

explanation: Placental hormone levels drop rapidly after delivery, not rise. Therefore, rising placental hormone levels are not a concern postpartum. [learn more](GNS121_U7_T7#GNS121_U7_T7_h6)

question: A patient recovering from a hip replacement cannot bend past 90 degrees. Which tool helps them put on shoes safely?

options.A: A four-wheeled walker
options.B: A standard metal cane
options.C: A set of axillary crutches
options.D: A long-handled shoehorn

explanation: Brilliant! A long-handled shoehorn lets them reach their feet easily without breaking their hip movement rules.

question: A patient has a roundworm infection. Which family of worms is responsible?

options.A: Trematodes
options.B: Nematodes
options.C: Cestodes
options.D: Bacteriodes

explanation: Well done! Roundworms belong to the nematode family, known for their smooth, cylindrical, unsegmented bodies.

question: How do secondary bone tumors differ from primary bone tumors?

options.A: Secondary tumors originate strictly from bone marrow cells
options.B: Secondary tumors are always benign growths that stop growing early
options.C: Secondary tumors only affect the cartilage and never the hard bone
options.D: Secondary tumors spread to the bone from another organ in the body

explanation: Think of secondary tumors as travellers. They started somewhere else like the breast or prostate and hitchhiked to the bones.

question: What is the term for a permanent alteration in the DNA sequence?

options.A: A mutation
options.B: A karyotype
options.C: A replication
options.D: A translation

explanation: A mutation is any change in the normal sequence of DNA nucleotides. [learn more](GNS111_U1_T7#GNS111_U1_T7_h5)

question: Which type of white blood cell is mainly responsible for the humoral immune response?

options.A: B cells
options.B: Red blood cells
options.C: Platelets
options.D: T cells

explanation: B cells run the humoral response! They mature into plasma cells that pump out helpful antibodies into your body fluids.

question: What medical term is used to describe specific blind spots inside a person's field of vision?

options.A: Cataracts
options.B: Diopters
options.C: Scotomas
options.D: Refractions

explanation: You're learning fast! Scotomas are small or large patches in the visual field where vision is reduced or completely missing.

question: Why is a multidisciplinary team necessary for managing advanced chronic pain?

options.A: Pain touches physical, emotional, and social aspects requiring diverse expertise
options.B: Nurses cannot assess pain intensity without a physiotherapist present
options.C: Doctors are not legally allowed to prescribe pain medicine without a pharmacist
options.D: Hospital accreditation rules require at least five professionals on every chart

explanation: Because total pain affects body, mind, and spirit, a team of medical, nursing, social, and spiritual experts provides the best comprehensive care. [learn more](GNS321_U4_T14#GNS321_U4_T14_h8)

question: Why is maintaining good musculoskeletal health so important for a patient?

options.A: It prevents all forms of infectious diseases
options.B: It completely stops the natural aging process
options.C: It preserves daily mobility and personal independence
options.D: It lowers the patient's blood pressure levels

explanation: Healthy bones, joints, and muscles allow a person to move freely and care for themselves without relying on others. [learn more](GNS222_U1_T25#GNS222_U1_T25_h1)

question: An anterior gishiri cut most directly puts which structure at risk of injury?

options.A: The anal sphincter
options.B: The coccyx bone
options.C: The cervix
options.D: The urethra and bladder

explanation: Cutting the anterior vaginal wall risks damaging the urethra and bladder wall, leading to urinary fistula formation. [learn more](GNS312_U1_T16#GNS312_U1_T16_h3)

question: How does well-integrated health data improve your daily nursing workflow?

options.A: It reduces time spent searching for records and supports proactive care
options.B: It prevents nurses from communicating directly with physicians
options.C: It forces nurses to spend all their shift fixing computer hardware
options.D: It removes all documentation requirements from the nursing shift

explanation: Having all your patient info connected in one place cuts down on annoying delays and helps you catch health problems before they turn into emergencies. You've got this! [learn more](GNS113_U2_T5#GNS113_U2_T5_h7)

question: A hospital pharmacy keeps cash from drug sales in an open drawer and uses it to buy office snacks, leading to empty shelves. Which part of the DRF system is failing?

options.A: Quantification and forecasting
options.B: Manufacturing of raw chemicals
options.C: Revenue collection and banking
options.D: Patient disease diagnosis

explanation: Makes total sense, right? If cash isn't banked safely and gets spent on snacks, the revolving fund stops revolving, and drugs run out!

question: A hospital wants to choose between two identical blood pressure drugs that work equally well and are equally safe. Which analysis should they use?

options.A: Cost-Benefit Analysis
options.B: Cost-Minimization Analysis
options.C: Cost-Effectiveness Analysis
options.D: Cost-Utility Analysis

explanation: Since the clinical effects are identical, you only need to compare their price tags. Cost-minimization helps you pick the least costly option.

question: Why does the early embryo divide multiple times without growing bigger in size?

options.A: To maintain a high concentration of oxygen within the cells
options.B: To fit through the narrow passage of the fallopian tube
options.C: To protect the inner cell mass from the harsh tubal fluid
options.D: To save all maternal nutrients for the later fetal stage

explanation: Brilliant! By dividing quickly inside a protective shell without growing in overall size, the tiny cells manage to travel safely down the tight fallopian tube.

question: A client comes to the clinic reporting pus, warmth, and increasing redness around her implant site five days after placement. What should you suspect?

options.A: A localized site infection requiring prompt medical evaluation and treatment
options.B: A sign that the implant has expired and needs immediate replacement
options.C: A normal healing reaction that proves the hormone is working effectively
options.D: A standard allergic reaction to the pressure bandage adhesive tape

explanation: Pus, warmth, and spreading redness are classic signs of a minor wound infection. It's nothing to panic about, but it definitely needs prompt cleaning and medical care!

question: A nurse teaches a patient with high blood pressure how to check their own BP at home. What is this called?

options.A: Permanent institutional placement
options.B: Maintenance and self-management support
options.C: Emergency trauma stabilization
options.D: Acute surgical intervention

explanation: Well done! Teaching patients to monitor their own chronic conditions helps them stay well and avoids sudden health emergencies.

question: What is a common result of having very restrictive abortion laws in developing countries?

options.A: Better funding and equipment for public maternity hospitals
options.B: Improved cooperation between traditional healers and doctors
options.C: The complete eradication of unintended pregnancies in society
options.D: An increase in dangerous, clandestine procedures performed by unqualified people

explanation: Correct. Making a procedure illegal doesn't stop it; it just drives desperate patients into secret, unsafe places.

question: Why should every task on a project checklist be assigned to a specific person?

options.A: To make it easier to fire workers who make minor mistakes
options.B: To ensure only the facility director does any actual work
options.C: To ensure accountability so responsibilities are never neglected
options.D: To prevent team members from communicating with each other

explanation: When everyone is responsible, no one is responsible! Assigning names ensures every important task actually gets done.

question: What is the medical term for blood collecting inside the pleural space?

options.A: Pleural effusion
options.B: Hemothorax
options.C: Chylothorax
options.D: Pneumothorax

explanation: You've got this! 'Hemo' means blood and 'thorax' means chest, so blood in the chest is a hemothorax.

question: A pregnant woman at 32 weeks is worried because a little yellowish fluid is leaking from her nipples. As a nurse, what do you tell her?

options.A: This means labor is likely to begin within the next forty-eight hours
options.B: This indicates a potential breast infection that requires antibiotic treatment
options.C: This is an abnormal finding caused by a drop in progesterone levels
options.D: This is a normal sign that the breasts are preparing to feed the baby

explanation: Reassure her! Spontaneous colostrum leaks late in pregnancy are completely normal and just mean the mammary glands are doing their job early.

question: What is the main objective of secondary prevention?

options.A: Early detection and prompt treatment of a disease to stop its progress
options.B: Providing end-of-life comfort care for terminally ill cancer patients
options.C: Promoting nationwide policies against tobacco farming and importation
options.D: Eliminating all genetic mutations that run in family lineages

explanation: Spot on! Secondary prevention is about catching a disease early through screenings so we can treat it quickly before complications arise.

question: What is a common misconception about the 'controlling' function in nursing?

options.A: That it is only performed once every ten years
options.B: That it has no role in preventing infections
options.C: That it exists purely to punish staff rather than improve systems
options.D: That staff nurses should never do quality audits

explanation: Controlling isn't about witch hunts! It's about spotting gaps in the system so we can fix them and do better.

question: How can severe physical or emotional stress lead to spaced-out periods (oligomenorrhoea)?

options.A: By suppressing hypothalamic release of GnRH
options.B: By causing immediate scarring of the uterine wall
options.C: By destroying ovarian follicles directly
options.D: By blocking estrogen receptors in the liver

explanation: Stress triggers hormones like cortisol, which temporarily puts a pause on the hypothalamus releasing GnRH. Without that signal, ovulation gets delayed!

question: A patient on chemotherapy calls the clinic saying their temperature is 38.5°C. What should you tell them to do?

options.A: Drink plenty of cold fluids and monitor the temperature for another day.
options.B: Apply a cool damp cloth to the forehead to bring down the fever.
options.C: Take a dose of paracetamol and rest in bed until tomorrow morning.
options.D: Come to the hospital immediately for a medical evaluation and blood work.

explanation: Fever in a chemo patient is an emergency because their immune system is low. Quick action can save a life!

question: Why do traditional beliefs often blame ancestral displeasure for psychological distress?

options.A: To show that physical injuries cause all brain disorders
options.B: To discourage individuals from talking to their neighbors
options.C: To prove that modern science has all the correct answers
options.D: To encourage people to maintain family traditions and moral codes

explanation: Makes total sense! Attributing illness to broken taboos or ancestral anger reinforces community morality and the importance of heritage.

question: Why is it a bad idea to put a hot water bottle on a patient's brand-new swelling?

options.A: It hardens the skin into a permanent scar
options.B: It stops all heart function and lowers blood pressure
options.C: It increases blood flow and can make the swelling worse
options.D: It immediately causes permanent skin freezing

explanation: Remember, heat opens things up! Putting heat on a fresh injury increases blood flow, making the swelling and bruising much worse.

question: Which finding strongly suggests a testicular rupture after a heavy blow to the scrotum?

options.A: Painless enlargement of both testicles over a period of several weeks
options.B: Clear watery drainage leaking from a small scratch on the scrotal skin
options.C: Loss of the normal outline of the testicle on ultrasound with severe local tenderness
options.D: Complete inability to control bowel movements after the impact

explanation: When the testicle bursts, it loses its smooth oval shape on an ultrasound scan, and the patient will have intense pain and swelling. You're mastering trauma assessments!

question: How do fake or substandard drugs make pharmacovigilance harder in places like Nigeria?

options.A: They eliminate the need for healthcare workers to monitor patients
options.B: They ensure that all adverse drug reactions are automatically reported to NAFDAC
options.C: They introduce unpredictable toxicities and therapeutic failures that distort safety data
options.D: They make clinical trials completely unnecessary for pharmaceutical companies

explanation: You got it! Counterfeit drugs cause weird reactions or simply fail to work, which completely throws off our tracking of how safe real medicines are.

question: What is the best way for a nurse to approach a community health program against FGM?

options.A: Avoid discussing the topic to prevent offending local traditions
options.B: Distribute dense medical research journals to every household
options.C: Scold village elders publicly for practicing barbaric customs
options.D: Explain physiological harms respectfully while engaging community leaders

explanation: Well done! Effective prevention relies on respectful, open dialogue that partners with local influencers.

question: How do somatic motor pathways typically reach their target muscles?

options.A: They operate completely without you ever knowing
options.B: They use a two-neuron chain with a ganglion in the middle
options.C: They only stimulate internal glands and organs
options.D: They use a single direct neuron straight to the muscle

explanation: That's right! Somatic pathways take a straight, fast path from the spinal cord straight to the skeletal muscle with no stops in between.

question: Which of these is NOT a normal market problem (imperfection) in healthcare?

options.A: Adverse selection where mostly sick people join insurance plans
options.B: Patients having perfect, expert knowledge of all complex medical treatments
options.C: Information asymmetry between the doctor and the patient
options.D: Moral hazard linked to having full health insurance

explanation: Well done! Patients definitely do *not* have perfect medical knowledge. The reality that patients lack this insider knowledge is actually a major market imperfection!

question: What is the very first thing you should do when starting a reproductive health chat with a patient?

options.A: Document the patient's exact insurance details
options.B: Ensure physical privacy and a quiet environment
options.C: Review previous laboratory blood test results
options.D: Immediately perform a full physical pelvic exam

explanation: You've got this! Patients need a private, safe space to feel comfortable discussing sensitive topics. Always secure a quiet, private spot first before diving into personal health questions.

question: Why should nurses take time to understand a patient's cultural or identity group?

options.A: Identity groups are the only source of funding for hospitals
options.B: It prevents patients from ever catching infectious diseases
options.C: Patients often follow health advice that respects their cultural norms
options.D: It allows the nurse to change the patient's religious beliefs

explanation: Spot on! When we respect a patient's cultural background, trust grows, and they are much more likely to follow our health guidance.

question: How does a rehabilitation nurse act as a bridge for the healthcare team around the clock?

options.A: By writing the medical diagnoses for the attending physician
options.B: By carrying daytime therapy goals into everyday 24-hour ward routines
options.C: By replacing the medical social worker during discharge meetings
options.D: By performing all physical and occupational therapy exercises alone

explanation: Nurses are at the bedside 24/7! We help make sure the skills patients learn during short therapy sessions are practiced all day long on the ward.

question: Why must a nurse know the exact landmarks of the vulva?

options.A: To pass a urinary catheter without missing the urethra
options.B: To prevent ovarian cysts
options.C: To measure blood pressure correctly
options.D: To track the exact day of ovulation

explanation: Spot on! Knowing your anatomy keeps procedures safe and stops you from accidentally placing a catheter into the vaginal opening instead of the urethra.

question: What does 'hypersensitivity' mean in sensory processing for an autistic patient?

options.A: Needing constant loud noises to feel comfortable
options.B: Being easily overwhelmed by normal sights, sounds, or touches
options.C: Being completely unable to feel any physical pain
options.D: Seeking out heavy objects to lift all day

explanation: Great job! Hypersensitive means their nervous system reacts extra strongly to everyday sounds, lights, or textures that others might easily ignore.

question: A mechanically ventilated patient suddenly experiences high-pressure alarms, low oxygen saturations, and absent breath sounds on the left side. Which emergency troubleshooting step comes first using the DOPE mnemonic?

options.A: Increase the oxygen concentration on the wall regulator
options.B: Immediately remove the breathing tube completely
options.C: Check for tube displacement or right mainstem intubation
options.D: Administer a dose of rescue bronchodilator medication

explanation: Sudden unilateral breath sound loss points directly to tube displacement, which must be assessed and corrected immediately. [learn more](GNS213_U2_T16#GNS213_U2_T16_h7)

question: What are the two main categories of nutrients required by the human body?

options.A: Water and dietary fiber
options.B: Macronutrients and micronutrients
options.C: Proteins and carbohydrates
options.D: Vitamins and minerals

explanation: Nutrients are divided into macronutrients, which are needed in large amounts, and micronutrients, which are needed in small amounts. [learn more](GNS227_U1_T005#GNS227_U1_T005_h1)

question: How do hookworm larvae usually get into the human body from dirty soil?

options.A: Active penetration through the skin
options.B: Bite from an infected mosquito vector
options.C: Inhalation of airborne dust particles
options.D: Ingestion of contaminated raw meat

explanation: Hookworm larvae love damp soil and can actually burrow right through the skin of bare feet or legs. Always good to remember why wearing shoes matters!

question: Why is a patient scheduled for an abdominal ultrasound usually told to fast (no food or water) for a few hours beforehand?

options.A: To keep their blood pressure steady before the scan
options.B: To cut down on tummy gas and keep the gallbladder full
options.C: To make sure they have an empty bladder for a pelvic check
options.D: To stop them from throwing up during the procedure

explanation: Food creates gas that blocks sound waves, and fasting keeps the gallbladder nice and full so it's easy to see!

question: Why is it so important to set clear learning objectives right at the start of a training program?

options.A: To satisfy legal requirements without needing to teach any practical skills
options.B: To ensure the program takes exactly eight hours to complete without failure
options.C: To give participants a clear goal of what they should achieve by the end
options.D: To prevent experienced nurses from attending the educational session

explanation: Clear objectives act like a roadmap. They let both the teacher and you know exactly what key takeaways to expect by the end of the session.

question: When testing deep tendon reflexes in a patient with hyperthyroidism, what do you expect to see?

options.A: Sluggish or absent reflexes
options.B: Unchanged normal reflexes
options.C: Hyperactive reflexes
options.D: Completely paralyzed limbs

explanation: Because excess thyroid hormone supercharges the nervous system, the reflexes will be brisk and hyperactive—jumpy reflexes match a jumpy metabolism!

question: What is usually the very first sign that a patient has taken in too much salt?

options.A: Severe yellow discoloration of the skin and eyes
options.B: Sudden and noticeable weight gain from fluid retention
options.C: Immediate development of a high grade fever
options.D: A sudden drop in resting heart rate below 50 beats per minute

explanation: You got it! Because water chases salt, eating too much sodium quickly shows up on the weighing scale as water weight.

question: What is the main job of counter-traction in a skeletal traction setup?

options.A: To double the amount of pulling force on the bone
options.B: To prevent the patient from sliding down and altering the pull
options.C: To keep the ropes from slipping out of the pulley grooves
options.D: To eliminate the need for regular pin site cleaning

explanation: Exactly! Counter-traction uses the patient's own body weight and gravity to pull in the opposite direction, keeping the traction steady and effective.

question: In a research framework, what is the dependent variable?

options.A: The presumed cause of the health problem
options.B: The outcome or effect being measured
options.C: The abstract mental image with no label
options.D: The personal opinion of the lead nurse

explanation: Remember: the dependent variable is your final result or outcome. It's what changes in response to whatever you are testing!
